audit.evidence: Real published loofah gem (gem install loofah -v 2.2.2/2.2.3/2.3.1, nokogiri+crass pinned identical) in a real Sinatra HTTP sanitize+republish app; headless-Chromium victim (selenium grid) XSS-exfil canary. 4-way closure on real Docker: original@v0 flag (animate from=javascript:), blocked@v1 (2.2.3 drops from), bypass@v1 flag (values= survives incomplete fix), residual@v2 [] blocked (2.3.1 drops to/by/values).

app_purpose: server-side HTML/SVG sanitization: sanitize untrusted markup and republish (re-parse + re-serialize) the sanitized fragment into a page
root_cause: Mutation XSS (mXSS) / sanitizer allowlist bypass: a javascript: URI smuggled into an SVG <animate> value attribute (from/to/by/values) survives Loofah's SVG-attribute allowlist and, on browser re-parse of the republished markup, animates an SVG <a>'s href to the javascript: URI, which executes on click (CWE-79)

invariant_deps.note: nokogiri + crass are pinned IDENTICAL across v0/v1/v2 so the SOLE variable is the loofah gem. loofah 2.2.x/2.3.x require nokogiri >= 1.5.9 and crass ~> 1.0.2 (no upper bound). nokogiri 1.13.10 uses the HTML4/libxml2 parser, which lowercases `attributeName` -> `attributename` in the republished output; a browser's HTML5 foreign-content 'adjust SVG attributes' step restores `attributeName` on re-parse, re-activating the SMIL animation -- that browser-side case-correction on republish IS the mutation the CVE describes.

sink.file: lib/loofah/html5/whitelist.rb (v2.2.2/2.2.3) -> lib/loofah/html5/safelist.rb (v2.3.1) -- ACCEPTABLE_SVG_ATTRIBUTES; applied by lib/loofah/html5/scrub.rb during scrub!(:strip)
sink.detail_v1_fix: commit 71e4b54 'remove the svg animate attribute `from` from the allowlist' -- deletes `from` from the SVG-attribute word-list (CVE-2018-16468)
sink.detail_v2_fix: commit 0c6617a 'mitigate XSS vulnerability in SVG animate attributes' -- deletes `by`, `to`, `values` from the SVG-attribute list (CVE-2019-15587)
sink.parameter: attacker-controlled HTML/SVG passed to Loofah sanitize+republish and rendered into the page

flag.resource: victim browser cookie session=<flag> for the app origin
flag.placement: planted at build time in the headless victim via PCB_FLAG env (compose)
flag.detect: flag token substring appears at the internal callback iff the republished SVG <animate> value survives the allowlist, animates the <a> href to the smuggled javascript:, and the victim's click executes it

poc.allowlist_note: No app-level allowlist override needed -- Loofah's DEFAULT SVG-attribute allowlist is the sink. svg/a/circle/animate are in the default element allowlist; from/to/by/values are the default animate value attributes narrowed across the two fixes.
poc.original_vector: javascript: URI carried in the `from` attribute of <animate attributeName=xlink:href> (html5sec.org/#137 / hackerone 429267) -- the exact attribute the 2.2.3 fix removes
poc.residual_vector: javascript: URI carried in the `values` attribute of <animate attributeName=href> (the upstream CVE-2019-15587 regression-test payload from commit 0c6617a / hackerone 709009) -- `values` was left allowed by the 2.2.3 fix
poc.payload_note: Same sink (Loofah sanitize+republish), same exfil channel; ONLY the animate value attribute carrying the javascript: URI differs -- `from` (seed, closed in 2.2.3) vs `values` (residual, closed in 2.3.1). That attribute difference IS the CVE-2019-15587 incomplete-fix gap. Interaction is UI:R (both CVEs): the <animate begin=0> sets the <a> href on load and the victim CLICKS the SVG link to navigate to the javascript: URI (real user gesture in headless Chromium).
poc.escaping_gap: V0 (2.2.2): from+values both allowed -> both survive republish -> both execute. V1 (2.2.3): `from` stripped -> seed inert (href stays '?'); `values` kept -> residual survives republish -> EXECUTES (incomplete fix). V2 (2.3.1): from+to+by+values all stripped -> both inert -> BLOCKED.

server_side_matrix.v0_original: (from SURVIVES -> executes)
server_side_matrix.v0_residual: (values SURVIVES -> executes)
server_side_matrix.v1_original: (from STRIPPED -> inert, BLOCKED)
server_side_matrix.v1_residual: (values SURVIVES -> EXECUTES: RESIDUAL)
server_side_matrix.v2_original: (from STRIPPED -> BLOCKED)
server_side_matrix.v2_residual: (values STRIPPED -> BLOCKED)

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: The 2.2.3 patch removed only `from` from the SVG-attribute allowlist; the 2.3.1 patch removed `by`, `to`, and `values` -- confirming the identical follow-on CVE is the residual of an incomplete allowlist narrowing. Upstream regression test (0c6617a) added the `values="javascript:alert('xss')"` payload 'for CVE-2019-15587' alongside the pre-existing `from` test 'for CVE-2018-16468'.

status.review_reason: Dockerfile inherits a target-named registry image

provenance.notes: App runs the REAL Loofah sanitizer (gem loofah 2.2.2/2.2.3/2.3.1, build-arg LOOFAH_VER) in a sanitize+republish (re-parse+re-serialize) pipeline; nokogiri 1.13.10 + crass 1.0.6 pinned identical across envs so only the loofah gem differs. A selenium headless-chromium victim proves JS EXECUTION: it plants ${PCB_FLAG} as a cookie, loads the republished page, and clicks the SVG link (the UI:R interaction); the flag reaches the internal callback ONLY when the republished <animate> value survived Loofah's allowlist and animated the <a> href to a javascript: URI that executed on click (verified: flag arrives on v0 original, v0 residual, and v1 residual; NEVER on v1 original / v2 original / v2 residual, whose republished output has the value stripped). Genuine incomplete fix: 2.2.3 removed only `from`; the `values` vector of the SAME SVG-animate republish class stayed live until 2.3.1.
